claim.text: We registered an OAuth app and used its authorize page straight away. GitHub asked for no review or approval.

evidence.quote: Registering needed one form submission. GitHub showed no review step, no CAPTCHA, no password re-prompt and no email confirmation.

summary: Self-serve, and we tested it: one form submission registered an app, and its authorize page worked right away, with no review. The real decisions are OAuth App versus GitHub App (GitHub recommends GitHub Apps) and how strictly to match redirect URLs, which GitHub changed recently.

composio.note: Composio lists a managed OAuth app for GitHub. You may not need your own unless you want your own branding, scopes beyond the defaults, or dedicated rate limits.

evidence.quote: Composio-managed OAuth available
| [GitHub](/toolkits/github.md) | `GITHUB` |

effort.text: 0.25-0.5 hours of developer work (estimate: one short web form, then wiring the callback URL into your app)

wait.text: No wait for registering an app: it worked immediately. (Marketplace listing was not tested.)

evidence.quote: The app's settings page loaded immediately.

claim.text: low (our judgment: no gated step is documented)

steps.text: Open Settings from your profile picture (top right of any GitHub page).

evidence.quote: click your profile picture, then click Settings

steps.text: In the left sidebar choose Developer settings, then OAuth apps.

evidence.quote: In the left sidebar, click Developer settings
In the left sidebar, click OAuth apps

steps.text: Click New OAuth App. On a first app the button reads Register a new application.

evidence.quote: this button will say, Register a new application

steps.text: Enter a homepage URL: the full URL to your app's website.

evidence.quote: type the full URL to your app's website
type the callback URL of your app

steps.text: Decide on Device Flow and on expiring user tokens (expiring tokens are on by default).

evidence.quote: Expire user access tokens is enabled by default.
Click Register application.

redirectRules.text: Up to 10 callback URLs per app.

evidence.quote: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs.

redirectRules.text: redirect_uri is optional. If you omit it, GitHub redirects to the first callback URL configured.

evidence.quote: The redirect_uri parameter is optional.
GitHub will redirect users to the first callback URL configured in the OAuth app settings.

redirectRules.text: With wildcard matching off, the redirect URL must exactly match a callback URL. It is configurable per callback URL.

evidence.quote: When wildcard matching is disabled, the redirect URL must exactly match the callback URL.

redirectRules.text: Apps with a single callback URL created before August 3, 2026 have wildcard matching on. Turn it off if you do not need it.

evidence.quote: Apps that had a single callback URL enabled prior to August 3, 2026 have wildcard matching enabled for that callback URL.

redirectRules.text: Loopback redirect URLs can use a different port than the registered callback URL.

evidence.quote: The redirect_uri does not need to match the port specified in the callback URL for the app.

redirectRules.text: For loopback, use 127.0.0.1 or ::1 rather than localhost.

evidence.quote: OAuth RFC recommends not to use localhost, but instead to use loopback literal 127.0.0.1 or IPv6 ::1

redirectRules.text: Tested: with wildcard matching off, a redirect_uri that adds a subpath to the registered one is rejected.

evidence.quote: http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/auth/callback/extra (subpath) | "The redirect_uri is not associated with this application."

redirectRules.text: Tested: a loopback redirect_uri with a different port than the registered one is accepted.

evidence.quote: http://127.0.0.1:5555/api/auth/callback (different loopback port) | Authorize screen: "Authorizing will redirect to http://127.0.0.1:5555"

redirectRules.text: Tested: an unrelated host is rejected.

evidence.quote: https://example.org/cb (unrelated host) | "The redirect_uri is not associated with this application."

requirements.text: Create the app under your personal account or any organization where you are an administrator.

evidence.quote: under your personal account or under any organization you have administrative access to

requirements.text: A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps.

evidence.quote: A user or organization can own up to 100 OAuth apps.

requirements.text: Only put information in the app that you consider public.

evidence.quote: Only use information in your OAuth app that you consider public.

gotchas.text: GitHub recommends building a GitHub App instead of an OAuth app.

evidence.quote: Consider building a GitHub App instead of an OAuth app.

gotchas.text: OAuth apps can only act on behalf of a user; GitHub Apps can also act independently.

evidence.quote: OAuth apps can only act on behalf of a user while GitHub Apps can either act on behalf of a user or independently of a user.

gotchas.text: If your code does not yet handle short-lived tokens, uncheck expiring tokens until it does.

evidence.quote: If your app's authentication code hasn't been updated to support short-lived tokens, uncheck the box until support is added.

gotchas.text: Wildcard callback matching is a security risk: it lets an attacker send authorization codes to any subdomain or subdirectory of the callback URL.

evidence.quote: Enabling wildcard matching can expose your app to security risks, because it allows an attacker to send authorization codes to any subdomain or subdirectory of the callback URL.

gotchas.text: PKCE, if you use it, must be S256. The plain method is not supported.

evidence.quote: Must be S256 - the plain code challenge method is not supported.

gotchas.text: GitHub Apps (not OAuth apps) can be registered from a manifest, but all three steps of the flow must finish within one hour.

evidence.quote: You must complete all three steps in the GitHub App Manifest flow within one hour.

gotchas.text: In the manifest flow, the person registering is redirected to a GitHub page where they confirm.

evidence.quote: The person registering the app will be redirected to a GitHub page with an input field

gotchas.text: The registration form says "Redirect URI" and offers per-URI wildcard matching, but GitHub's creation guide still says "Authorization callback URL".

evidence.quote: The registration form labels the field "Redirect URI", with the button "Add redirect URI", not "Authorization callback URL".

gotchas.text: New apps show warnings on the consent screen: not owned by GitHub, created less than a day ago, fewer than 10 users.

evidence.quote: Created less than a day ago" and "Fewer than 10 GitHub users

gotchas.text: Defaults on the form: wildcard matching off, device flow off, expiring user tokens on.

evidence.quote: Allow wildcard matching: off
Expire user access tokens: on

surfaceClaim.text: We created the app by filling in and submitting GitHub's web form. The docs we read describe no API for it.

evidence.quote: Filled four fields through the page's form controls: application name, homepage URL, description, one redirect URI.

agentCan.text: Fill in and submit the registration form once the account is signed in.

evidence.quote: Clicked Register application.

agentCan.text: Check the redirect rules by requesting the authorize URL with different redirect_uri values, no credentials needed.

evidence.quote: Requested GitHub's authorize URL four times with different redirect_uri values to see which are accepted.

youMust.text: Sign in to GitHub, and pass 2FA if it is on. The agent cannot enter credentials.

evidence.quote: Signing in to GitHub (and 2FA, if enabled) is the account owner's job. The agent cannot enter credentials.

youMust.text: Each end user must click Authorize on the consent screen. We stopped before that step.

evidence.quote: Each end user must click Authorize on the consent screen. This was not exercised.

sources.title: Creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs
Registering a GitHub App from a manifest - GitHub Docs

gaps: We tested a personal-account OAuth app only: not an organization-owned one, and not a GitHub App.
We did not generate a client secret or run a token exchange, and we did not try the Marketplace listing path.
The docs neither confirm nor rule out an API for creating OAuth apps. We only know the web form works.
Scope documentation (Scopes for OAuth apps) was not reviewed for this guide.
